limitations: Fabric: each compute->pool link is a FIFO byte server and the pool is a shared byte server (aggregate pool service never exceeds pool bandwidth).
Requests larger than local DRAM spill their overflow pages to the pool (swap_remote only); a spilled newest page makes each KV append a fabric write.
Closed-loop: the issuing request blocks until its transfer completes, so queue_depth_bytes backpressure is inherent; excess is still reported as queue_overflow_events / backpressure_stall_ns.
Percentiles come from a log-bucket histogram (upper bucket edge, <=1% relative error, never under-reports).

policy.fallback_reason: 'hot_cold' is a later-phase policy; 'swap_remote' ran instead

scenario_assumptions: Local DRAM and CXL values are starting presets from docs/HARDWARE-MODELS.md, not measurements of a specific machine.
Each compute-to-pool link is modeled as an independent byte server; shared pool service contention is not yet modeled in this revision.
The workload is synthetic KV-cache decode derived from Llama-3-70B geometry. It is not a captured serving trace.
Results are relative comparisons between policies until the scenario is calibrated against measured latency distributions.
warnings: policy.name: 'hot_cold' arrives in Phase 3; falling back to 'swap_remote' and recording the fallback in the manifest
